title: Insider Threat Correlation — IT Manager on Shift

fields.organization: North Coast Regional Airport Authority — IT & Cybersecurity
fields.location: Main Server Room, Rack 4; Field Panels (Terminal Zones A & B)
fields.summary: Cross-referencing network logs, PACS system events, and physical access anomalies from the past 48 hours reveals a consistent temporal correlation between all system disruptions and the shift schedule of IT Manager Jordan Kelley. During all flagged incidents — rogue device on VLAN 30, 4-hour log gap on core switch, hot server closet at Room 217, door propped open — Kelley was the sole IT staff on duty. No other staff member was logged in or active on the network during these events. The pattern suggests a single point of access and control. No external breach indicators found. Internal access remains unchallenged.

findings.notes: User 'jkelley' logged in at 13:10, 13:30, and 13:55. No other IT staff were active in the session logs for the same period.
Device first detected at 13:18. Last activity logged at 13:45. Active only during Kelley’s shift window (13:00–14:30). No other IT team member had access to VLAN 30 configuration.
Log gap from 10:00 PM to 2:00 AM on 10/21/2026. Correlates with Kelley’s shift end. No system reboot recorded. Network traffic resumed normally.
Heat spike detected at 13:42. Door was found propped open at 13:58. Access logs show badge 'SEC-BADGE-01' used at 13:50. No other access logs from IT staff after 13:40.
Local Mode engaged on 4 panels (T1–T4) at 13:52. No formal order issued. Manual override logs show no override activity.
SEC-BADGE-01 (NCIA-ENROLL) was accessed at 13:48. No record of badge issuance or revocation. Last successful login by 'jkelley' was at 13:47.
No tampering. All 30-day recordings intact.
Last sync to NCIA-PACS-REPL at 13:45. No anomalies.
All doors in Fail-Secure mode. No unauthorized unlock events.
No unauthorized cabling or jacks found.

actionsTaken: Reviewed PACS server logs and user session history
Cross-referenced network events with IT shift logs
Verified badge access and device MAC correlation
Notified IT Team Lead via encrypted chat (14:14)
Initiated internal audit of all IT access points
recommendations: Immediately isolate Jordan Kelley from network access and PACS systems
Preserve all server logs, access records, and device images as forensic evidence
Initiate internal investigation under airport policy 7.3 (Insider Threat Protocol)
Contact Airport Security and Legal for escalation to FBI/CISA per TIRP 13.4
Do not confront Kelley directly; secure the network before any action
fields.photosNote: 5 photos attached: IMG_FIR20260419-001 (PACS server log screen), IMG_FIR20260419-002 (VLAN 30 device MAC), IMG_FIR20260419-003 (Room 217 thermal scan), IMG_FIR20260419-004 (badge access log), IMG_FIR20260419-005 (shift log correlation chart)

instructorNote: This inject forces the team to confront the insider threat directly. Watch for hesitation in isolating Kelley, or attempts to bypass procedures. The team must now decide whether to act on evidence or await policy guidance.
